title: A human cell, part by part
alt: A human cell cut open: its membrane with proteins, the nucleus with its pores and chromatin, rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, the Golgi apparatus, mitochondria, lysosomes, the centrosome and the fibres of the cytoskeleton.

scale.note: The membrane, its proteins, the pores, ribosomes, fibres and centrioles are drawn larger than they are

parts.name: Cell membrane
parts.note: encloses the cytoplasm, protects the cell and controls what goes in and out.

parts.name: Membrane proteins
parts.note: span the membrane: channels and pumps that let things in and out, and receptors that pass on signals.

parts.name: Cytoplasm
parts.note: the jelly-like fluid that fills the cell, where most of its work is done; the organelles sit in it.

parts.name: Nuclear envelope
parts.note: two membranes with many pores, through which substances pass between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

parts.name: Nuclear pores
parts.note: gates through the double wall of the nucleus: messenger RNA, copied from the DNA, leaves through them. A real nucleus has thousands.

parts.name: Chromatin
parts.note: in the nucleus; it holds the DNA, the genetic material that directs the life of the cell.

parts.name: Nucleolus
parts.note: a dense round body in the nucleus, where the parts of ribosomes are made.

parts.name: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
parts.note: flattened sacs joined to the nuclear envelope, studded with ribosomes; they make proteins and carry them through the cell.

parts.name: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
parts.note: a network of tubes without ribosomes: it makes fats and stores calcium.

parts.name: Ribosomes
parts.note: very small grains without a membrane, where proteins are made; free in the cytoplasm or on the rough ER.

parts.name: Golgi apparatus
parts.note: a stack of curved, flattened sacs that receives, modifies, packs and sends out the cell's products.

parts.name: Transport vesicles
parts.note: small sacs budding off the Golgi apparatus, carrying products to where they are used or to the membrane.

parts.name: Lysosomes
parts.note: small sacs with one membrane, holding enzymes that break down substances, worn-out organelles and bacteria.

parts.name: Centrosome
parts.note: two centrioles at right angles, each a ring of nine triplets of microtubules; the cell’s microtubules grow out from around them.

parts.name: Mitochondrion
parts.note: two membranes, the inner one folded into cristae; where most of cellular respiration takes place, releasing energy for the cell.

parts.name: Microtubules
parts.note: hollow tubes of protein that grow out from the centrosome: tracks along which motor proteins carry cargo.

parts.name: Actin filaments
parts.note: the thinnest fibres, a mesh under the membrane that shapes the cell’s edge and lets it move.

parts.name: Intermediate filaments
parts.note: tough fibres like rope, from the nucleus to the membrane: they hold the cell together under strain.

steps.title: One human cell
steps.text: About 20 micrometres across: a bag of watery cytoplasm, its parts each with a job. Cut open here to show them.

steps.title: Cell membrane
steps.text: A film of fats, two layers thick, with proteins set in it: gates that let things in and out.

steps.title: Nucleus
steps.text: Stores the DNA, the instructions for making proteins: about two metres of it, drawn here as loose thread.

steps.title: Nuclear pores
steps.text: Gates through the wall of the nucleus. Messenger RNA, a copy of a gene, leaves through them for the ribosomes.

steps.title: Rough ER
steps.text: Folded membranes round the nucleus, studded with ribosomes, which make proteins.

steps.title: Smooth ER
steps.text: A network of tubes without ribosomes: it makes fats and stores calcium.

steps.title: Golgi apparatus
steps.text: Finishes, sorts and ships proteins, in small vesicles.

steps.title: Mitochondria
steps.text: Use oxygen to turn food into ATP, the cell’s fuel. A real cell has hundreds, often in a network.

steps.title: Lysosomes
steps.text: Bags of acid and enzymes that break down worn-out parts.

steps.title: Cytoskeleton
steps.text: Fibres of protein that shape the cell and carry its cargo: microtubules, actin filaments and intermediate filaments.

steps.title: Centrosome
steps.text: Two centrioles at right angles, each nine triplets of microtubules: the cell’s microtubules grow out from here.
